\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پمپ} \fa{بنزین} (pomp-e benzin)}{پمپ بنزین (pomp-e benzin)}]{\fa{پمپ} \fa{بنزین} (pomp-e benzin) — a petrol station (US: gas station)}

\label{lesson:FA-C423-pomp-e-benzin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to start, then the Persian for to stall.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پمپ} \fa{بنزین}}
\textbf{\fa{پمپ} \fa{بنزین}} (\emph{pomp-e benzin}) — \textquotedblleft{}a petrol station (US: gas station)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{این} \fa{جاده} \fa{پمپ} \fa{بنزین} \fa{کم} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar in jâdde pomp-e benzin kam ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There are few petrol stations on this road.
\end{quote}

Literally 'petrol pump'. In speech also \emph{pomp benzin}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pomp-e benzin} is built from \emph{pomp} 'pump', a European loan usually traced to French \emph{pompe}, and \emph{benzin} 'petrol', usually traced to French \emph{benzine}. EtymDB does not list the compound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pomp-e benzin}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pomp-e benzin}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pomp-e benzin}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to start, then the Persian for to stall, then say \emph{pomp-e benzin} again
\end{itemize}

What does \fa{پمپ} \fa{بنزین} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A petrol station (US: gas station)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بنزین} \fa{زدن} (benzin zadan)}{بنزین زدن (benzin zadan)}]{\fa{بنزین} \fa{زدن} (benzin zadan) — to fill up (with petrol), to get petrol}

\label{lesson:FA-C423-benzin-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to stall, then the Persian for a petrol station.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بنزین} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{بنزین} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{benzin zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to fill up (with petrol), to get petrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{سفر} \fa{بنزین} \fa{زدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Qabl az safar benzin zadim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We filled up before the trip.
\end{quote}

\emph{benzin} + \emph{zadan}. Present stem \emph{zan-}: \emph{benzin mizanim} — we fill up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{benzin zadan} is built from \emph{benzin} 'petrol', usually traced to French \emph{benzine}, and the native verb \emph{zadan} 'to strike'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to stall, then the Persian for a petrol station, then say \emph{benzin zadan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باک} (bâk)}{باک (bâk)}]{\fa{باک} (bâk) — a fuel tank (of a car)}

\label{lesson:FA-C423-bak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a petrol station, then the Persian for to fill up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باک}}
\textbf{\fa{باک}} (\emph{bâk}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fuel tank (of a car)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{باک} \fa{ماشین} \fa{تقریبا} \fa{خالی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bâk-e mâshin taqriban khâli ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car's tank is almost empty.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bâk râ por kardan} — to fill the tank. A different, older \emph{bâk} means fear.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâk} 'fuel tank' was borrowed from Russian and is usually traced to Russian \emph{bak} 'a tank'. EtymDB lists Russian \emph{bak} only with a different, nautical sense, so the line is hedged.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâk}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâk}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a petrol station, then the Persian for to fill up, then say \emph{bâk} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{باک} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fuel tank (of a car)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تمام} \fa{شدن} (tamâm shodan)}{تمام شدن (tamâm shodan)}]{\fa{تمام} \fa{شدن} (tamâm shodan) — to run out; to be finished, to end}

\label{lesson:FA-C423-tamam-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to fill up, then the Persian for a fuel tank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تمام} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{تمام} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{tamâm shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to run out; to be finished, to end\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{وسط} \fa{جاده} \fa{بنزین} \fa{ما} \fa{تمام} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Vasat-e jâdde benzin-e mâ tamâm shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our petrol ran out in the middle of the road.
\end{quote}

\emph{tamâm} 'complete, finished' + \emph{shodan}. \emph{Tamâm kardan} is to finish something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tamâm shodan} is built from \emph{tamâm} 'complete, finished', borrowed from Arabic \emph{tamām} 'complete' (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tamâm shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to fill up, then the Persian for a fuel tank, then say \emph{tamâm shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کارواش} (kârvâsh)}{کارواش (kârvâsh)}]{\fa{کارواش} (kârvâsh) — a car wash}

\label{lesson:FA-C423-karvash}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fuel tank, then the Persian for to run out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کارواش}}
\textbf{\fa{کارواش}} (\emph{kârvâsh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a car wash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جمعه} \fa{ماشین} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{کارواش} \fa{بردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jom'e mâshin râ be kârvâsh bordim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
On Friday we took the car to the car wash.
\end{quote}

A loan word, said as in English.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kârvâsh} was borrowed from English and is usually traced to English \emph{car wash}. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
